plan.chapterName: OpenStax University Physics, chapter 14: Fluid Mechanics
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a shaded perspective drawing of a clear cylindrical container partly filled with a pale blue liquid. The vessel has an elliptical rim with a thick rounded glass lip, a slightly darker band marking the liquid surface a short way down, and a darker pooled region across the curved bottom. Three small cubes outlined in black dashed lines sit at different places within the liquid, each drawn in the container's perspective and each carrying a numeral: cube 1 high and toward the left, cube 2 a little lower and to the right, and cube 3 near the bottom center. A curved arrow links each cube to its own label, written as a ratio in tall parentheses with a subscript, reading Δm/ΔV with subscript 1 at the upper right, Δm/ΔV with subscript 2 at the middle right, and Δm/ΔV with subscript 3 out to the left. Giving each sampling cube its own subscripted mass-to-volume ratio invites the reader to treat the three as separate numbers rather than one value for the whole vessel, which is how local density is defined point by point.

elements: transparent cylindrical glass container with vertical side walls
thick pale cyan elliptical top rim and inner opening ellipse
faint rear wall of the transparent cylinder visible through the liquid
pale blue liquid volume filling most of the cylinder but stopping below the rim
horizontal elliptical liquid surface near the upper part of the vessel
darker blue elliptical pooled region at the curved bottom of the liquid
three dashed black wireframe sampling cubes immersed in the liquid
numeral 1 centered inside the upper-left sampling cube
numeral 2 centered inside the middle-right sampling cube
numeral 3 centered inside the lower-center sampling cube
curved black leader arrow from upper-right label to cube 1
curved black leader arrow from middle-right label to cube 2
curved black leader arrow from left label to cube 3
math label (Δm/ΔV)_1 at the upper right of the cylinder
math label (Δm/ΔV)_2 at the middle right of the cylinder
math label (Δm/ΔV)_3 to the left of the lower half of the cylinder
highlight outline and translucent fill for the currently selected sampling cube
selected-sample readout showing ΔV, Δm, and Δm/ΔV beside the clicked cube

interactions.teaches: Density is evaluated at a chosen local region: clicking cube 1, 2, or 3 treats that small dashed volume as the sample around one point in the fluid

interactions.label: Sample cube side length
interactions.teaches: As the cube shrinks, both Δm and ΔV decrease, while their ratio approaches the local point density at that cube's position

interactions.label: Fluid model
interactions.teaches: A uniform liquid gives the same mass-to-volume ratio everywhere, while a heterogeneous liquid gives different local ratios at cubes 1, 2, and 3

demo_steps.title: Three local samples
demo_steps.narration: The three dashed cubes mark small volumes around different points in the liquid. Click any cube to highlight it and read its local Δm/ΔV ratio.

demo_steps.title: Shrink the sample volume
demo_steps.narration: Reducing the side length makes the selected ΔV smaller. The displayed Δm changes with it, but Δm/ΔV settles toward the density at that point.

demo_steps.title: Compare with a uniform liquid
demo_steps.narration: Switching to a uniform liquid makes all three sampled ratios match. There is then one bulk density rather than a position-dependent local density.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: World-space layout: cylinder axis vertical along +Y, centered at X=0, Z=0. Cylinder radius about 1.15 units, glass height 3.1 units from Y=0 to Y=3.1, liquid height about 2.45 units from Y=0.15 to Y=2.6. The view is nearly front-on with a slight look from above so the top rim and liquid surface appear as ellipses. Use +X screen-right, +Y screen-up, +Z receding away from the viewer. Top rim is a torus or nested ellipses: outer radius 1.22, tube/rim thickness about 0.08, colored pale cyan #cceff2 with alpha about 0.45. Glass side wall is a transparent cylinder shell #bdebf0 with alpha 0.22, with stronger side-edge strokes. Liquid is a translucent cylinder #b9d8f5 with alpha about 0.55; liquid surface ellipse #d8eaff alpha 0.75; bottom pooled ellipse darker #5faed1 alpha 0.35. Cube positions: cube 1 at approximately X=-0.45, Y=1.85, Z=0.05; cube 2 at X=0.52, Y=1.35, Z=0.0; cube 3 at X=0.02, Y=0.62, Z=0.12. Default cube side length 0.32 units; all cubes are axis-aligned with faces parallel to the X/Y/Z axes, rendered as black dashed wireframe edges. Numerals are black, centered on the front face of each cube. Label positions in screen/world overlay: (Δm/ΔV)_1 sits outside the cylinder at upper right near X=1.55, Y=2.05; (Δm/ΔV)_2 sits outside at middle right near X=1.6, Y=1.25; (Δm/ΔV)_3 sits left of the vessel near X=-1.8, Y=1.0. Curved leader arrows are black with arrowheads pointing toward the corresponding cubes. Density model: for Uniform use rho=1000 kg/m^3 everywhere. For Heterogeneous use a smooth field such as rho(x,y,z)=930 + 115*(2.5-y) + 85*x + 70*exp(-((x-0.05)^2+(y-0.55)^2+(z-0.1)^2)/0.22) kg/m^3, clamped to remain positive. For a selected cube with side s, ΔV=s^3 and Δm should be computed as the numerical average of rho over the cube times ΔV; show Δm/ΔV as that average density. The point-density limit is rho at the cube center.
interactionPlan.notes: Use transparent rendering with depth sorting carefully: draw the liquid before dashed cube edges and labels so the cubes remain readable through the fluid. Render math labels and curved arrows as screen-space SVG or CSS2D overlays locked to 3D anchor points; keep the visual proportions close to the source figure rather than physically exact optics. On click, thicken the selected cube's dashed edges, add a faint yellow fill #ffd84d with alpha 0.18, and show a compact readout near that cube. In Uniform mode, all symbolic labels may remain visible but the selected readout should make clear that cubes 1, 2, and 3 have equal Δm/ΔV. In Heterogeneous mode, tint the liquid very subtly with a vertical/positional blue gradient so the distinct local densities are visually motivated without obscuring the original pale blue style.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Click to sample a cube: the learner clicks cube 1, 2, or 3, the selected dashed volume highlights and its Delta m / Delta V ratio appears beside it, showing that density is evaluated locally at the chosen point.
- Slider for sample-volume size: the learner shrinks or enlarges the selected cube, the measured mass and volume change while the local ratio tends toward a point value, clarifying how local density comes from a small surrounding volume.

authoredContext:
The density of a substance is not necessarily constant throughout the volume of a substance. If the density is constant throughout a substance, the substance is said to be a homogeneous substance. A solid iron bar is an example of a homogeneous substance. The density is constant throughout, and the density of any sample of the substance is the same as its average density. If the density of a substance were not constant, the substance is said to be a heterogeneous substance. A chunk of Swiss cheese is an example of a heterogeneous material containing both the solid cheese and gas-filled voids. The density at a specific location within a heterogeneous material is called local density, and is given as a function of location, ρ=ρ(x,y,z) (the figure).

Density may vary throughout a heterogeneous mixture. Local density at a point is obtained from dividing mass by volume in a small volume around a given point.

Figure is a drawing of a container filled with a liquid. Small cubes are drawn in different regions of the container to indicate local density points.

Local density can be obtained by a limiting process, based on the average density in a small volume around the point in question, taking the limit where the size of the volume approaches zero,

discrepancies: A prominent extra numeric readout callout for Cube 1 is added inside the beaker, which is not present in the source and partially obscures the simple textbook composition.
The selected cube is filled with a pale yellow highlight, whereas all source cubes are only dashed outlines with numbers.
The liquid is rendered with extra heterogeneous horizontal bands and a stronger bottom pool tint; the source shows a simpler uniform blue liquid with only subtle top and bottom ellipses.
Cube 3 is placed closer to the center/front-bottom than in the source, where it sits lower-left relative to the other samples.
The arrows are somewhat muted/gray in places and less like the clean black curved leader arrows in the source.
evaluation.notes: The generated figure is clearly recognizable and conceptually accurate, but it adds interactive readouts, highlighting, and density bands that make it busier than the original simple diagram.

Remove or greatly reduce the yellow selected-cube fill when matching the static source figure.
Simplify the liquid appearance by removing the extra heterogeneous bands unless an interaction explicitly enables them.
Adjust Cube 3 slightly lower-left to better match the original placement.
